title: America 250 Quiz: Test yourself on presidents, power and pivotal moments
dek: As America prepares to celebrate its 250th anniversary, test your knowledge of the commanders in chief who helped shape the nation.

questions.prompt: Who was the first president of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington became the first U.S. president in 1789 and remains the only president unanimously chosen by the Electoral College.

questions.prompt: Who was the first president to live in the White House?
questions.explanation: John Adams moved into the unfinished Executive Mansion in 1800. George Washington selected the site but never lived there.

questions.prompt: Which president approved the Louisiana Purchase in 1803?
questions.explanation: Thomas Jefferson's administration purchased the Louisiana Territory from France, dramatically expanding the size of the United States.

questions.prompt: Which president delivered the Gettysburg Address?
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address in 1863, dedicating a cemetery at the Pennsylvania battlefield.

questions.prompt: Which president served more than two terms in office?
questions.explanation: Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected four times. The 22nd Amendment later limited presidents to two elected terms.
Andrew Jackson earned the nickname "Old Hickory" from soldiers who compared his toughness to hickory wood.

questions.prompt: Which president had been a Hollywood actor before entering national politics?
questions.explanation: Ronald Reagan appeared in films and television before serving as California governor and later as the 40th president.

questions.prompt: Which president signed the Emancipation Proclamation?
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation during the Civil War; it took effect on Jan. 1, 1863.

questions.prompt: Who was the youngest person ever elected president of the United States?
questions.explanation: John F. Kennedy was 43 when elected in 1960. Theodore Roosevelt became president at 42 after William McKinley's assassination, but he was not first elected at that age.

questions.prompt: Which president signed the act creating the National Park Service in 1916?
questions.explanation: Woodrow Wilson signed the Organic Act in 1916, establishing the National Park Service within the Department of the Interior.
